scores.evidence: Critical path: access/IAM → Argo CD + config repos → pilot to prod → chart/workflow contract v1 (M2) → onboarding throughput → legacy shutdown
scores.rationale: Phases run from identity/infra substrate up to onboarding and enforcement, with spikes proving unknowns before the contract is frozen and Kyverno enforcement waiting for 50/50.

scores.evidence: One low-risk pilot service goes from merge to production through the real pipeline. A prod rollback is demonstrated in under 10 minutes.
scores.rationale: M1 is a real thin slice to prod with approval and rollback before the golden path and features.

scores.evidence: D2 ... Hard (all deploy config shaped around it) | Revisit if: Not on Kubernetes (A1)
scores.rationale: A decision table lists options, reversibility, and revisit triggers, and assumptions carry defaults and impact-if-wrong.

scores.evidence: Tier-1 services come last, once the platform has 30 services of history.
scores.rationale: Shared components (OIDC, Argo CD, chart, workflows) precede leaf services; the canary group and render-diff limit blast radius, and leaf onboarding goes from low risk to tier-1.

scores.evidence: Security (built in M1; signing M2; enforcement M4)
scores.rationale: Security is concrete in M1 (OIDC, no keys, gitleaks, protected prod repo) and in M2 and M4, but M3 has little security work and it is mostly a standalone section.

scores.evidence: From M1: Argo CD metrics into Prometheus. Alerts: prod app Degraded for more than 10 min → owning team
scores.rationale: Alerts and Slack deploy messages are in M1, followed by workflow metrics in M2, delivery metrics in M3, and canary analysis in M4.

scores.evidence: Each service is built once into a container image that never changes and is identified by its digest
scores.rationale: Immutable digests, Terraform infra, pinned actions, versioned charts and GitOps state are reproducible from M1, and Argo CD is rebuilt from Git.

scores.evidence: T14 Write and drill rollback ... decision → previous digest healthy ≤ 10 min; break-glass dry run in staging
scores.rationale: Rollback, retries, ancestry checks and PreSync migration handling are in M1; HA and rebuild drills are in M3; tag rollback and canary aborts are in M2 and M4.

scores.evidence: AI-specific concerns: not applicable. There are no AI components.
scores.rationale: The plan explicitly declares the AI layer N/A and adds no AI components.

scores.evidence: Ephemeral PR environments | Staging contention reported by > 3 teams
scores.rationale: The deferred table has concrete pull-forward triggers for each item, and the plan also lists deliberate shortcuts and non-goals.

note: Very strong, well-sequenced plan with a thin prod slice first; the only weak spot is security, which is thin in M3 and partly a standalone section.
